assumptions: The rule binds the RECORD, not a runtime. It refuses an unbounded law; it does not make a bounded one true.
ASM-MEDIATION-UNIVERSE is itself undischarged — the rule requires that the obligation exist and be named, never that it be met.
attrs.evidence: R4.1's discipline, applied to R7.3's finding: when an error is mechanical, make the refusal mechanical. check-mosaic.mjs §12 resolves admission_mediation.universe.ref as a dotted path into mosaic/embodiment.json and admission_mediation.universe.discharge_obligation against mosaic/assumptions.json, requires both declared laws to be present with DISTINCT enforceability, and requires exactly one of them to be mechanically enforceable and exactly one to be architectural. Three registered mutations run on every invocation with a positive control: deleting the universe, pointing its ref at a path that does not resolve, and collapsing the two laws back into one enforceability so the architectural half reads as checkable. All three are refused; the unmutated registry is not.
attrs.prior_art: MEDIATION-UNIVERSE-BOUND is the proposition; this is the enforcement. Same split as ASR-DEFEATER-ACTIVITY (the citation) versus ASR-ACTIVE-UNRESOLVED (the adoption).

readjudicated.method: witness_reran_on_target — the named gate executes here and is green in this candidate's gate run
readjudicated.note: The source-lane status is recorded in imported_from.source_status as provenance. This field records that the TARGET lane re-established it; the two are separate facts and the gate reads this one.

attrs.review_focus: This proves that the record cannot state an unbounded mediation law. It does not prove the universe is complete, and the third mutation exists because the likeliest way to lose this is not deleting the universe but quietly re-merging the two laws so the whole thing reads as enforced again.
attrs.statement: A mediation law recorded in this artifact must name a universe that resolves and a discharge obligation that resolves, and a law whose universe is absent is refused.
